# unifi_qos_rule (Resource)

The `unifi_qos_rule` resource manages a UniFi QoS rule (Quality of Service). QoS rules prioritize or rate-limit matched traffic on a WAN/VPN network — for example the built-in *Critical Apps Prioritization* rule.

## Example Usage

```terraform
# Prioritize a set of applications on the primary WAN.
resource "unifi_qos_rule" "critical_apps" {
  name               = "Critical Apps Prioritization"
  enabled            = true
  objective          = "PRIORITIZE"
  download_burst     = "OFF"
  upload_burst       = "OFF"
  wan_or_vpn_network = unifi_network.wan.id

  schedule = {
    mode = "ALWAYS"
  }

  source = {
    matching_target = "ANY"
  }

  destination = {
    matching_target    = "APP"
    port_matching_type = "ANY"
    app_ids            = [393220, 393245]
  }
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `name` (String) The name of the QoS rule.

### Optional

- `destination` (Attributes) The traffic destination matched by the rule. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--destination))
- `download_burst` (String) Whether download burst is enabled. One of `ON`, `OFF`.
- `enabled` (Boolean) Whether the rule is enabled. Defaults to `true`.
- `index` (Number) The evaluation order of the rule. Lower is evaluated first.
- `objective` (String) The QoS objective for matched traffic, e.g. `PRIORITIZE`.
- `schedule` (Attributes) An optional schedule constraining when the rule is active. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--schedule))
- `site` (String) The name of the UniFi site where this resource should be applied. If not specified, the default site will be used.
- `source` (Attributes) The traffic source matched by the rule. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--source))
- `upload_burst` (String) Whether upload burst is enabled. One of `ON`, `OFF`.
- `wan_or_vpn_network` (String) The id of the WAN or VPN network the rule applies to.

### Read-Only

- `id` (String) The unique identifier of this resource.

<a id="nestedatt--destination"></a>
### Nested Schema for `destination`

Optional:

- `app_category_ids` (List of Number) Application category ids matched when `matching_target` is `APP_CATEGORY`.
- `app_ids` (List of Number) Application ids matched when `matching_target` is `APP`.
- `ips` (List of String) IP addresses matched when `matching_target` is `IP`.
- `matching_target` (String) What the destination matches on. One of `ANY`, `APP`, `APP_CATEGORY`, `IP`, `NETWORK`, `REGION`, `WEB`.
- `network_ids` (List of String) Network ids matched when `matching_target` is `NETWORK`.
- `port_matching_type` (String) How ports are matched. One of `ANY`, `SPECIFIC`, `OBJECT`.
- `regions` (List of String) Regions matched when `matching_target` is `REGION`.


<a id="nestedatt--schedule"></a>
### Nested Schema for `schedule`

Optional:

- `date` (String) A single date (`YYYY-MM-DD`) for one-time schedules.
- `date_end` (String) The end date (`YYYY-MM-DD`) of the schedule window.
- `date_start` (String) The start date (`YYYY-MM-DD`) of the schedule window.
- `mode` (String) The schedule mode. One of `ALWAYS`, `EVERY_DAY`, `EVERY_WEEK`, `ONE_TIME_ONLY`, `CUSTOM`.
- `repeat_on_days` (Set of String) Days of the week the schedule repeats on (`mon`..`sun`).
- `time_all_day` (Boolean) Whether the rule is active the entire day.
- `time_range_end` (String) The end time (`HH:MM`) of the active window.
- `time_range_start` (String) The start time (`HH:MM`) of the active window.


<a id="nestedatt--source"></a>
### Nested Schema for `source`

Optional:

- `client_macs` (List of String) Client MAC addresses matched when `matching_target` is `CLIENT` or `MAC`.
- `ips` (List of String) IP addresses matched when `matching_target` is `IP`.
- `matching_target` (String) What the source matches on. One of `ANY`, `CLIENT`, `NETWORK`, `IP`, `MAC`, `REGION`.
- `network_ids` (List of String) Network ids matched when `matching_target` is `NETWORK`.
- `port_matching_type` (String) How ports are matched. One of `ANY`, `SPECIFIC`, `OBJECT`.
- `regions` (List of String) Regions matched when `matching_target` is `REGION`.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
# import from provider configured site
terraform import unifi_qos_rule.critical_apps 694009322cd2eb1c05176d01

# import from another site
terraform import unifi_qos_rule.critical_apps another-site:694009322cd2eb1c05176d01
```
